chosen.premise: When Raichu’s electric pouches run empty, it raises its tail to pull electricity from the atmosphere.
chosen.hook: What does Raichu do when its batteries run out?
chosen.visualIdea: Show an empty battery icon, then Raichu’s raised tail drawing lightning from storm clouds.
chosen.note: A highly specific and genuinely strange recharge rule: empty pouches lead to a raised tail gathering atmospheric electricity. The battery-to-storm visual makes the premise instantly understandable.

candidates.premise: Raichu can exceed 100,000 volts—enough for one strike to incapacitate a Copperajah.
candidates.hook: One Raichu shock could drop an elephant Pokémon.
candidates.visualIdea: Put Raichu’s voltage beside a Copperajah silhouette as the shockwave knocks it out.
candidates.note: A precise, high-impact comparison backed by the Legends: Arceus entry; however, the hook risks overstating voltage as a direct measure of knockout power.

candidates.premise: Raichu’s electricity is also a mood meter: the more it stores, the more aggressive it becomes.
candidates.hook: Raichu doesn’t just store electricity—it stores stress.
candidates.visualIdea: Show an electricity gauge filling as Raichu shifts from calm to visibly aggressive.
candidates.note: The Pokédex directly links stored electricity to aggression and even frames the buildup as stress; the mood-gauge visual is clear, though the general idea is somewhat anthropomorphic.

candidates.premise: Raichu is rarely seen for a strange reason: Trainers prefer Pikachu’s appearance.
candidates.hook: Raichu’s biggest rival might be its own pre-evolution.
candidates.visualIdea: Place Pikachu in the spotlight while Raichu fades into the background, then reverse the focus.
candidates.note: The official entry gives this an unusually candid premise, and the Pikachu-versus-Raichu framing is surprising. It is more social commentary than a visual mechanic.

candidates.premise: Raichu uses its tail as a ground wire, discharging excess electricity to protect itself from its own power.
candidates.hook: Raichu’s tail is basically a built-in lightning rod.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate electricity flowing from Raichu’s body down its tail into scorched ground.
candidates.note: Strongly supported and easy to animate, but the built-in grounding-tail concept is less surprising than Raichu’s other mechanics.

candidates.premise: Raichu’s evolution chain switches rules: Pikachu needs friendship, but Raichu needs a Thunder Stone.
candidates.hook: Raichu’s evolution changes from friendship to an item.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a friendship meter filling for Pikachu, then a Thunder Stone triggering Raichu’s evolution.
candidates.note: Concrete and well structured, but evolution-method contrasts are familiar to many fans and the method data comes from trusted secondary research rather than a cited Pokédex entry.

rounds.request: N/A—the selected angle is strong enough. Stronger alternatives would need an equally specific Raichu-only rule, a surprising contradiction or number, direct research support, and a visual transformation that can be understood immediately.
